official.description_text:
Postdoc in Acoustics-Based Traffic Sensing
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences
Job description
Join KTH's research in engineering acoustics at the Marcus Wallenberg Laboratory (MWL) and develop the next generation of acoustics-based traffic sensing. Cost-effective roadside microphones, combined with signal processing and machine learning, can provide continuous, real-time information on traffic flows, vehicle types and traffic noise, whereas cities today rely on short and intrusive measurement campaigns.
The position is part of two projects funded by
Digital Futures
, carried out together with the City of Stockholm, Nacka municipality and other municipalities in the region: a societal innovation project expanding an acoustic sensor network across the Stockholm region, and a proof-of-concept project developing a validated roadside monitoring system. You will build on established testbeds and unique datasets from Stockholm's urban environment.
You will deploy acoustic sensor units in urban environments, develop robust methods for detecting and classifying vehicle pass-bys, from processing on the sensor (edge) to the cloud, validate the results against reference measurements, and make data available through APIs and visualisation tools for municipal users. The position also includes scientific publishing, co-supervising students and contributing to new proposals and innovation activities.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Strong background in at least two of the following areas: acoustic measurements, signal processing, machine learning, sensor systems or embedded systems.
Documented research experience through scientific publications.
Good programming skills, for example in Python.
Proficiency in English, both written and spoken, as it is used in daily work.
As a person, you are curious, independent and motivated by research with practical impact. You demonstrate:
Teaching abilities
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Independence
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Experience with acoustics-based traffic monitoring or with detection and classification of vehicles from sound.
Experience deploying sensors or measurement systems in the field over long periods.
Experience with machine learning for audio or time-series data, including deployment on edge devices.
Experience with data pipelines, databases, APIs or web-based visualisation.
Previous collaboration with non-academic stakeholders (municipalities, government agencies, industry).
Interest in innovation and in the utilisation of research results.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: 2-year postdoctoral position at KTH (Marcus Wallenberg Laboratory, Engineering Acoustics) developing acoustic sensor networks for urban traffic monitoring. Work combines signal processing, machine learning, embedded systems, field deployment, and municipal stakeholder engagement across Stockholm region. Funded by Digital Futures; collaboration with city and municipalities.

thematic_fit.rationale: Adjacent but not aligned. The position concerns real-world sensor deployment, infrastructure monitoring, and urban data pipelines—not human-centred interaction, spatial learning, or immersive systems. However, the emphasis on user-facing (municipal) applications, practical systems thinking, and real-world validation shares methodological values with human-centred research. The researcher's target domain (immersive learning, wayfinding) involves spatial understanding; traffic sensing is tangentially spatial (urban environment monitoring) but not immersive, collaborative, or learning-focused.

methodological_fit.rationale: Moderate methodological fit. Both roles require signal processing, machine learning for classification (vehicle detection from audio ≈ spatial/behavioural pattern recognition in immersive systems), sensor systems thinking, and field validation. The researcher has intermediate quantitative-research, experimental-design, and (implied) systems integration from the XR orientation project. Both roles emphasise real-world grounding and stakeholder engagement. However, the position requires advanced embedded systems, edge computing, and audio signal processing—domains where the researcher has no demonstrated expertise. The methodological foundations overlap; execution skill gaps are substantial.

growth_value.rationale: Moderate growth value, but sideways rather than forward. The researcher would develop signal processing, machine learning deployment on edge devices, large-scale field data pipelines, and stakeholder collaboration—valuable general research skills. However, these do not advance the core target competencies: spatial cognition theory, collaborative immersive interaction design, or human-centred XR methodology. The researcher emerges with stronger systems thinking and ML skills, but no deeper expertise in immersive learning or spatial understanding research.

strategic_value.rationale: Strong strategic value for location and funding, moderate value for domain trajectory. KTH is a top institution in Sweden (Priority 1 preferred country). Digital Futures funding, 2-year postdoc contract, and Stockholm municipality partnerships offer visibility and professional development. However, the position does not build standing in immersive HCI or XR research networks. A postdoc in acoustic traffic sensing does not establish credentials for future HCI faculty roles. The position is prestigious but off-domain; it expands the researcher's technical toolkit without anchoring doctoral/postdoctoral identity in the target field.

eligibility_flags: Researcher is not yet postdoctoral (MSc in progress). Position requires PhD by the time employment decision is made; ineligible until PhD awarded.
Posting specifies 'A doctoral degree or equivalent, obtained within the last three years' as preferred qualification. Researcher would need to complete PhD and apply within 3 years of defence.
Security clearance mention ('security-sensitive role' under Protective Security Act 2018:585): researcher's Malaysian background and international mobility may trigger additional vetting.

Position requires 'strong background in at least two of: acoustic measurements, signal processing, machine learning, sensor systems, embedded systems.' Researcher has intermediate machine learning (implicit in ML tasks in XR project) but no formal training; borderline on 'strong.'
risks: Researcher is not yet postdoctoral; significant eligibility gap.
No background in signal processing or acoustic measurement. Steep retraining curve; first 6–9 months would be foundational learning, not productive research.
Security clearance requirement may delay or block appointment depending on national/institutional policy applied to Malaysian citizens.
2-year fixed-term postdoc; no pathway to permanent academic position at KTH or continuation of immersive HCI research.
Postdoc in acoustic sensing establishes credentials in sensor systems and embedded ML, not immersive HCI. Future faculty searches in HCI/XR may view fit as peripheral.
If PhD is pursued in immersive HCI/XR (aligned domain), postdoc in traffic acoustics creates a CV narrative gap: 'Why sensors after HCI doctoral training?'
